newsitem.title: USA: Texas utility may sell up to $600 mln of debt.
newsitem.headline: Texas utility may sell up to $600 mln of debt.

text.p: City Public Service, a municipal utility in San Antonio, Texas, plans to sell up to $600 million of tax-exempt municipal bonds, an official there said Friday.
Donald Thomas, manager of financial services for City Public Services, said while the deal could come to market as early as May, plans remain in the early stages and further approvals are needed.

"There are a number of steps necessary before that transaction would occur," he said. "It requires City of San Antonio approval to issue any bonds on behalf of City Public Service, and we have not been through that step as yet, and won't be for a few weeks."
Thomas said the utility received approval from its board on April 24 to proceed with additional paper work on the deal.
Proceeds from the bonds would be used for new construction, and, depending on market rates, for a potential advance refunding, he said.

PaineWebber Inc. and Smith Barney Inc. are expected to be co-senior managers on the offering, with PaineWebber serving as bookrunner, Thomas said. Approximately 15 other firms are involved as well, he said.
City Public Service currently has approximately $2.7 billion of long-term debt and just under $300 million of short-term debt outstanding, Thomas said.
